domain.decoder: the key data.values: 3,584 JSON numbers read as the IEEE-754 doubles they denote (the platform's own parse), the heights of equal steps of width 1/1792 on [0, 2]; as published Σ h_i exceeds n/2, so the heights are scaled by (n/2)/Σ h_i, a scale-down that keeps 0 <= h <= 1 and makes ∫ h = 1 exactly (the record's reading, rescaled: true); the keys id, agentName, score and createdAt are the platform's metadata, not the domain

g.named: sup_x ∫ h(t) (1 − h)(x + t) dt = (2/n) · max_m Σ_i a_i (D − a_{i+m}) / D^2 for the n-step function with integer numerators a_i over the common denominator D, g = 1 − h on [0, 2] and both zero outside (the maximum over every lag m; the overlap is piecewise linear with knots on the grid)

reference: the bar is the 1b page's printed 0.3808585749 taken exactly (the platform's score prints 0.3808585748578584); the quantity is the overlap of the pinned heights read as doubles and normalised to mass 1, the record's exact value 0.380858574857858309…, below the bar by 4.2e-11; the registry row cites the leaderboard, so the bytes are the platform's API object for solution 2507 as pinned 2026-10-02 (the 2026-10-18 fetch returned the same values)
hypotheses: the definition on the 1b page: C_1b is the largest constant with sup_{x in [-2,2]} ∫_{-1}^{1} f(t) g(x+t) dt >= C_1b for all f, g: [-1,1] → [0,1] with f + g = 1 and ∫ f = 1 (extended by zero), so one admissible f gives C_1b <= its overlap with g = 1 − f (read)

the translation of [-1, 1] to [0, 2] leaves the supremum unchanged, and for equal steps the overlap is piecewise linear in x with knots on the grid, so the supremum is attained at a grid shift (read; relied on by the decider)
falsifier: the overlap of the normalised heights computed exactly exceeds 3808585749/10000000000
the published heights sum to at most n/2 (then the normalisation is not a scale-down and the decider refuses) or a normalised height is outside [0, 1]
